1.1: Back when the judges was runnin' things, a bad famine hit the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah took his wife and two sons and moved to Moab to try and make it.
1.2: That man was Elimelech, his wife was Naomi, and they had two sons—Mahlon and Chilion—both from Bethlehem, Judah. They packed up and settled in Moab.
1.3: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, passed away, leavin' her with just her two sons.
1.4: The sons got married to Moabite women—one named Orpah, the other named Ruth. They was livin' in Moab for about ten years.
1.5: Then both Mahlon and Chilion died too, leavin' Naomi all alone, without her husband or her sons.
1.6: Naomi heard that God had looked out for His people back home, blessin' them with food again. So she got up, ready to leave Moab and go back.
1.7: She started the journey with her two daughters-in-law, leavin' Moab and headin' toward Judah.
1.8: On the way, Naomi turned to them and said, 'Y'all go on back to your mama's house. May the Lord bless y'all like y'all blessed my sons and me.'
1.9: 'I pray the Lord give y'all new husbands, so y'all can rest easy in a good home.' Then she kissed them, and they all broke down cryin'.
1.10: They told her, 'Nah, we ain't leavin' you. We goin' back with you to your people.'
1.11: But Naomi said, 'Ain't no point in y'all followin' me. I can't give y'all no more sons to marry.'
1.12: 'Go on back, my daughters. I'm too old to be somebody's wife again. And even if I did get married tonight and had more sons—'
1.13: 'Would y'all wait for them to grow up? Would y'all stay single just for them? No, my daughters, this ain't right. The Lord got His hand against me, and it hurts me to see y'all go through this too.'
1.14: They all started cryin' again. Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye, but Ruth held on tight.
1.15: Naomi told her, 'Look, your sister-in-law goin' back to her people and her gods. You should go with her.'
1.16: But Ruth said, 'Don't tell me to leave you or stop followin' you. Where you go, I'ma go. Where you stay, I'ma stay. Your people my people, and your God my God.'
1.17: 'Where you die, I'ma die, and that's where they gon' bury me. May the Lord deal with me harshly if anything but death separates us.'
1.18: When Naomi saw Ruth wasn't budgin', she stopped tryin' to convince her.
1.19: So the two of them made it to Bethlehem. When they got there, the whole town was buzzin', like, 'Ain't this Naomi?'
1.20: But she told them, 'Don't call me Naomi no more. Call me Mara, 'cause the Almighty done made my life real bitter.'
1.21: 'I left here full, but the Lord brought me back empty. Why y'all callin' me Naomi when God done brought this struggle on me?'
1.22: So Naomi came back to Bethlehem with Ruth, the Moabite. They got there just as the barley harvest was startin'.

2.1: Now, Naomi's late husband had a rich relative from Elimelech's side of the family. His name was Boaz.
2.2: One day, Ruth—who was from Moab—told Naomi, 'Let me go out to the fields and pick up leftover grain from whoever's field I find favor in.' Naomi said, 'Go 'head, my daughter.'
2.3: So Ruth went out to the fields, pickin' up the leftovers behind the workers. By chance, she ended up in a field that belonged to Boaz, who was kin to Elimelech.
2.4: While she was out there, Boaz rolled up from Bethlehem and greeted the workers, 'The Lord be with y'all!' They called back, 'The Lord bless you!'
2.5: Boaz spotted Ruth and asked his supervisor, 'Who she belong to?'
2.6: The supervisor said, 'That's the young Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from Moab.'
2.7: 'She asked if she could gather grain behind the workers, and she been at it all day—only took a short break inside.'
2.8: Then Boaz went to Ruth and said, 'Listen, my daughter, don't go work in nobody else's field. Stay right here and stick close to my women.'
2.9: 'Keep your eyes on the field where they workin' and follow behind. I already told my men not to mess with you. And if you get thirsty, go on and drink from the water they pulled up.'
2.10: Ruth fell down, bowed low, and said, 'Why you bein' so kind to me? I'm just a foreigner.'
2.11: Boaz told her, 'I heard all about what you done for Naomi since your husband passed. You left your mama, your daddy, and your home to come live with folks you ain't never met before.'
2.12: 'May the Lord bless you for all that work. May the God of Israel pay you back in full, since you done put yourself under His protection.'
2.13: Ruth said, 'I hope I stay in your good graces, sir. You done made me feel safe and spoke kind to me, even though I ain't one of your servants.'
2.14: When it was time to eat, Boaz told her, 'Come eat with us. Dip your bread in the vinegar.' She sat down with the workers, and he made sure she got roasted grain to eat. She ate good and even had some left over.
2.15: When she got up to go back to work, Boaz told his men, 'Let her pick grain even from the good bundles, don't say nothin'.'
2.16: 'Matter of fact, drop some extra grain on purpose so she can gather more—don't check her about it.'
2.17: Ruth worked all day, then beat out what she gathered—it came out to about an ephah of barley.
2.18: She carried it all back to town, and Naomi saw how much she had gathered. Then Ruth pulled out the extra food she had saved from lunch and gave it to Naomi.
2.19: Naomi asked her, 'Girl, where you been workin' today? Who looked out for you like this? Whoever it was, may the Lord bless them!' Ruth told her, 'I was workin' in this man's field—his name Boaz.'
2.20: Naomi smiled and said, 'Oh, the Lord is good! He ain't stopped showin' love to the livin' and the dead. Boaz is one of our family redeemers!'
2.21: Then Ruth added, 'Boaz told me to stay close to his workers until the whole harvest is done.'
2.22: Naomi told Ruth, 'That's real good, my daughter. Stay in his field, so folks don't bother you somewhere else.'
2.23: So Ruth kept workin' with Boaz's women, gleanin' until the barley and wheat harvests was finished. And she kept livin' with Naomi.

3.1: One day, Naomi told Ruth, 'My daughter, I gotta find you a good home, somewhere you'll be taken care of.'
3.2: 'Now, Boaz—the man whose field you was workin' in—he's family. And guess what? He gon' be at the threshin' floor tonight, workin' on the barley.'
3.3: 'So here's what you do—wash up, put on some perfume, and wear your best outfit. Then go down to the threshin' floor, but don't let him see you until he done eatin' and drinkin'.'
3.4: 'When he lays down to sleep, pay attention to where he lay. Then go, pull back the blanket at his feet, and lay there. He'll tell you what to do next.'
3.5: Ruth said, 'Alright, I'ma do everything you said.'
3.6: So Ruth went down to the threshin' floor and did just like Naomi told her.
3.7: After Boaz finished eatin' and drinkin', he was feelin' good. He went to lay down by the pile of grain. Ruth came in quiet, uncovered his feet, and laid down.
3.8: Around midnight, Boaz woke up startled. He turned over and—boom!—a woman was layin' at his feet.
3.9: He said, 'Who's there?' Ruth answered, 'It's me, Ruth, your servant. Cover me with your robe, 'cause you my family redeemer.'
3.10: Boaz said, 'May the Lord bless you, my daughter! You coulda chased after young men—rich or broke—but instead, you stayed loyal to family.'
3.11: 'Don't worry, I'ma do right by you. Everybody in town know you a good woman.'
3.12: 'Now, it's true I'm family, but there's another man closer in line than me.'
3.13: 'Stay here tonight. If he wanna step up and marry you, then cool. But if he don't, I swear on the Lord, I'ma do it. Now, go 'head and lay down till morning.'
3.14: So Ruth laid there till morning, but got up before it was light enough for folks to recognize her. Boaz told her, 'Don't let nobody know you was here at the threshin' floor.'
3.15: Then he said, 'Hold out your shawl.' She did, and he filled it with six measures of barley, put it on her, and sent her back to town.
3.16: When Ruth got home, Naomi asked, 'How'd it go, my daughter?' Ruth told her everything Boaz did for her.
3.17: She said, 'He gave me all this barley and told me, "Don't go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed."'
3.18: Naomi said, 'Now sit tight, my daughter. This man ain't gon' rest till he settles this matter today.'

4.1: Boaz went up to the city gate and sat down. Then that other family redeemer—the one Boaz talked about—just so happened to walk by. Boaz called out, 'Hey man, come sit down for a minute.' So dude sat down.
4.2: Then Boaz got ten city elders together and said, 'Y'all sit down too.' So they did.
4.3: Boaz told the other guy, 'Naomi just came back from Moab, and she's sellin' the land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.'
4.4: 'I wanted to let you know so you can buy it back if you want to, right here in front of these elders. If you wanna redeem it, go 'head. But if not, let me know, 'cause after you, I'm next in line.' The man said, 'Aight, I'll redeem it.'
4.5: Then Boaz said, 'But if you buy the land from Naomi, you also gotta take Ruth—the Moabite widow—so the family name and inheritance stay intact.'
4.6: The man thought about it and said, 'I can't do it, that'll mess up my own inheritance. You go 'head and redeem it, I can't take that on.'
4.7: Now back in the day, when folks in Israel made a deal like this, they'd take off their sandal and hand it over as a way to seal the agreement.
4.8: So the other man told Boaz, 'You buy it then,' and took off his sandal.
4.9: Boaz turned to the elders and everybody around and said, 'Y'all are witnesses today—I'm buyin' everything that belonged to Elimelech, Mahlon, and Chilion from Naomi.'
4.10: 'And I'm takin' Ruth—the Moabite widow of Mahlon—as my wife, so his name don't get erased from his family line. His name gon' live on at the city gate. Y'all witness this today.'
4.11: Then all the people at the gate, plus the elders, said, 'We witnesses! May the Lord bless this woman coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, who built up Israel. May you be prosperous in Ephrathah and make a name for yourself in Bethlehem!'
4.12: 'And may your family be like Perez's, the one Tamar had with Judah, all 'cause of the child the Lord gon' give you through Ruth.'
4.13: So Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed them with a son.
4.14: The women told Naomi, 'Praise the Lord! He ain't left you without a family redeemer today. May this child's name be famous in Israel!'
4.15: 'He gon' restore your life and take care of you in your old age, 'cause your daughter-in-law—who love you and is better than seven sons—gave birth to him.'
4.16: Naomi took the baby, held him close, and became like a second mama to him.
4.17: The neighborhood women said, 'Naomi got a son now!' And they named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, who was the father of David.
4.18: Now here's the family line from Perez: Perez had Hezron.
4.19: Hezron had Ram, and Ram had Amminadab.
4.20: Amminadab had Nahshon, and Nahshon had Salmon.
4.21: Salmon had Boaz, and Boaz had Obed.
4.22: Obed had Jesse, and Jesse had David.
